purpose: Close the smallest possible syndrome-compression shortcut. Prove that on every connected loopless graph with nonzero cycle rank, every nonzero one-dimensional GF(3) linear projection of the graphic sign-cube syndrome is surjective onto GF(3). Hence a rank-one hash always has a zero preimage, even on an uncolourable graph where the true full syndrome never vanishes.

setup.graph: A connected loopless graph G=(V,E) with cycle rank beta=|E|-|V|+1>0.
setup.cycle_matrix: Q is any beta by |E| full-row-rank GF(3) matrix whose row space is the cycle/flow space ker(B), where B is an oriented incidence matrix.
setup.syndrome: S(Q)={Q s : s in Sigma} subset GF(3)^beta.
setup.rank1_hash: For nonzero lambda in GF(3)^beta, h_lambda(y)=lambda^T y in GF(3).

nonzero_cycle_support.statement: Every nonzero vector a in ker(B) has support size at least two in a loopless graph.
nonzero_cycle_support.proof: If support(a)={e} for a nonloop edge e=uv, the incidence equation at u contains the single nonzero contribution +/-a_e and cannot equal zero. Thus a one-edge nonzero flow is impossible. In a simple graph the support is in fact at least three, but two is all the theorem needs.

two_sign_sum.statement: For any two nonzero coefficients a,b in GF(3), the set {a eps + b delta : eps,delta in {+1,-1}} is all of GF(3).
two_sign_sum.proof: Every nonzero GF(3) coefficient is +/-1. Multiplying a sign by a or b therefore still ranges over {+1,-1}. The sums 1+1=2, 1+(-1)=0 and (-1)+(-1)=1 realize all three residues.

theorem.name: EVERY_NONZERO_RANK1_GRAPHIC_SIGN_SYNDROME_CHARACTER_IS_SURJECTIVE
theorem.statement: For every nonzero lambda in GF(3)^beta, {lambda^T Qs : s in Sigma}=GF(3).
proof: Put a=lambda^T Q. Because Q has full row rank and lambda is nonzero, a is a nonzero vector in row(Q)=ker(B).
By the support lemma, a has at least two nonzero coordinates e,f.
Vary s_e and s_f while temporarily fixing all other signs. The two varying terms a_e s_e+a_f s_f already attain all three residues by TWO_SIGN_SUM.
The contribution of all fixed remaining signs is one constant translation in GF(3), which preserves the full three-element image.
Therefore the complete sign cube maps surjectively onto GF(3).
theorem.zero_corollary: For every nonzero lambda there exists s in Sigma with lambda^T Qs=0.
theorem.uncolourable_false_positive: If G is not 3-colourable, v5.2 says there is no s with Qs=0. Nevertheless every rank-one hash has some s with lambda^T Qs=0. Thus every one-character compressed zero-test accepts a false positive on every loopless cyclic uncolourable graph.

relation_to_safe_kernel.kernel: A rank-one hash h_lambda has kernel D=lambda^perp, a codimension-one subspace of syndrome space.
relation_to_safe_kernel.v5_6_condition: Strong zero reflection requires D intersect (S(Q)-{0})=empty.
relation_to_safe_kernel.consequence: The theorem says this is impossible on an uncolourable loopless cyclic graph: D always contains at least one attainable syndrome, and because genuine zero is unattainable that syndrome is nonzero.
relation_to_safe_kernel.meaning: Any sound linear compression of such an UNSAT graphic instance that still performs a zero test must retain at least two correlated syndrome coordinates. A single GF(3) character can never certify non-colourability.

killed: Compress the full cycle syndrome to one nonzero GF(3) linear functional and test whether the projected value can be zero.
Search over polynomially many one-dimensional characters hoping one becomes a sound UNSAT separator; every nonzero character is individually surjective.
Use one parity/checksum coordinate as a zero-reflecting substitute for all mixed cycle equations on a loopless cyclic hard source.
not_killed: Rank-two-or-higher correlated projections whose kernel is proved source-specifically safe.
Nonlinear hashes or contractions with an exact zero-reflection theorem.
Interlacement/transition-matroid constructions that do not reduce to one linear character.
scope_firewall.loop_note: Loops are excluded intentionally. A loop is already an immediate obstruction to proper vertex colouring and also permits a one-edge cycle-space vector; the NP-hard Hamiltonian sources are simple/loopless.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_RANK2_SYNDROME_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION_V5_8
next_target.directive: Classify two-dimensional projections H Q of the sign cube. PG(1,3) has only four projective column directions, so derive an exact finite-state characterization of when 0 is absent/present in {H Qs}. Use that characterization to test whether rank-two projections can yield polynomially discoverable safe kernels on Hamiltonian C4 source graphs, without enumerating the original sign cube.
